=={{header|Omegese}}==
{{works with|omc|sha256 2c824805, aien-dev/omega-mv e5b32567, Linux AArch64}}
Omega has no imports, so the small output helpers (<code>emit</code> and friends) are part of the program.
<syntaxhighlight lang="text">
om2
text nl "\n"
text phi "phi("
text eqs ") = "
text prm ", prime"
text cnt "primes up to "
text col ": "
note ph n is Euler's totient of n for n up to 100000
global ph ulong 100001
note emit writes every byte of a to stdout; a short write is retried, an error exits 1
fn emit a view uchar * to void
o = ulong 0
while lt o len a bound 4096
k = write 1 a o sub len a o
if le k 0
exit 1
end
o = add o ulong k
end
end
note emitu writes n in decimal; 20 digits hold every ulong
fn emitu n ulong to void
d = new uchar 20 0
i = ulong 20
v = n
while true bound 20
i = sub i 1
put d i uchar add rem v 10 48
v = div v 10
if eq v 0
break
end
end
emit part d i sub 20 i
end
note sieve: start with ph n = n; each prime p (still ph p = p when reached) scales its multiples by (1 - 1/p)
note bound: each p touches at most 100000 / p multiples
fn sieve to void
for i ulong 100001
put ph i i
end
p = ulong 2
while le p 100000 bound 100000
if eq get ph p p
j = p
while le j 100000 bound 100000
put ph j sub get ph j div get ph j p
j = add j p
end
end
p = add p 1
end
end
note n > 1 is prime exactly when phi(n) = n - 1
fn main to int
sieve
for i ulong 25
n = add i 1
emit phi
emitu n
emit eqs
emitu get ph n
if eq get ph n sub n 1
emit prm
end
emit nl
end
lim = ulong 100
c = ulong 0
for i ulong 99999
n = add i 2
if eq get ph n sub n 1
c = add c 1
end
if eq n lim
emit cnt
emitu lim
emit col
emitu c
emit nl
lim = mul lim 10
end
end
ret 0
end
</syntaxhighlight>
{{out}}

phi(5) = 4, prime
phi(6) = 2

phi(8) = 4
phi(9) = 6
phi(10) = 4
phi(11) = 10, prime
phi(12) = 4
phi(13) = 12, prime
phi(14) = 6
phi(15) = 8
...
phi(22) = 10
phi(23) = 22, prime
phi(24) = 8
phi(25) = 20

primes up to 10000: 1229
primes up to 100000: 9592
